title.rendered: Be Alert and of Sober Mind: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
Be alert and of sober mind. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour. Resist him. Stand firm in the faith. You are not alone. The whole family of God is going through the same.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, June 26, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Be alert and of sober mind. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour. Resist him, standing firm in the faith, because you know that the family of believers throughout the world is undergoing the same kind of sufferings.”
1 Peter 5:8-9 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Peter writes 1 Peter to believers scattered across what is now Turkey, undergoing real persecution. He could have written a soft, encouraging letter. Instead, near the end of the letter, he gives them the warning the church has always needed and rarely wants to hear. Your enemy is real. He is hunting. Be alert.

The Greek phrase Peter uses is nepho. To be sober. To be clear-headed. The opposite of intoxicated. He is not just talking about literal drinking. He is talking about the spiritual sobriety that lets a believer see what is actually going on. The intoxicated mind, the distracted mind, the lazy mind, the mind that is just drifting through life, is the mind that gets ambushed. The sober mind sees the lion before it pounces.

That image, the roaring lion looking for someone to devour, is striking on purpose. Peter wants you to feel the weight of it. The enemy is not a cartoon villain. He is not a metaphor. He is a real, active, intelligent personal evil who walks the earth looking for believers to take down. He prowls. He waits. He looks for the moment of distraction, the area of pride, the unhealed wound, the unguarded relationship, the unconfessed sin. He uses whatever opening he can find.

And Peter’s response is not panic. It is sobriety. Be alert. See clearly. Refuse to live in a fantasy where the spiritual world is not real. Take seriously what the New Testament takes seriously. The believer who lives soberly is the believer the lion has the hardest time devouring.

But Peter does not stop with the warning. He gives the practical step. Resist him. Standing firm in the faith. The same Greek word for resist is the word for digging in your heels and refusing to be moved. The believer does not fight the lion by being clever. They fight the lion by standing on what they already know is true. The faith already given. The promises already made. The Saviour already enthroned. From that ground, the lion cannot devour.

And Peter ends with the line that matters most for the discouraged. You are not the only one going through this. The whole family of believers across the world is undergoing the same kind of sufferings. The persecution in Northern Iraq. The mockery in secular London. The pressure in the corporate office in Lagos. The discouragement in the small church in rural Nebraska. It is one family. One enemy. One Saviour. One war. And the war is being won, soul by sober soul.

Prayer

Father, make me sober-minded today. Lift the fog. Sharpen my spiritual sight. Help me see where the enemy is prowling around my life and resist him standing firm in the faith. Strengthen me through the knowledge that I am not alone. The global family of believers stands with me. The same Spirit who fortifies them fortifies me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am alert and of sober mind. I see what is actually going on in the spiritual realm. I refuse to be ambushed. I resist the devil, standing firm in the faith. I am not alone. The family of believers around the world stands with me, and the Lord stands over all of us.
